   {
    "title": "Reset is still accepted while a usable value depends on an access to an old emission: the K.Invalidates/KA fix covers only descendants of the anchor",
    "severity": "major",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:2118-2120 (ResetPre), 2254-2255 (ArenaResetContract), 2292 (KA); interacts with exitG 574-577; report formal/reports/MM03_v0.1.md:34 (row K.Invalidates), :121, :287",
    "cause": "Formalization error. After the fix, ArenaResetContract (which KA now satisfies) means: reset invalidates the anchor and the anchor's descendants. ResetPre clause 1 only checks the authorities listed in ar.issued. When the frame holding an issued block exits, exitG moves an active access derived from that block onto `internal` (decision (c) 14). That access is then neither an issued authority nor a descendant of the anchor, and MM-03.3.6 transitivity through anchors is not represented. So a value that depends on the access survives reset.     "evidence": "Spec §6 reset: « Aucune autorité émise encore active ni aucune valeur dépendante encore utilisable ne serait invalidée par la réinitialisation » and « une région encore effectivement utilisée ne peut être invalidée par reset ». §11 case 7 expects « Rejet ». Before the exit, `r5.ancs 6 = [5, 1]` and `ResetStep KA r2.2 r5 .reject` holds. `¬ (6 = anchor ∨ anchor ∈ r7.ancs 6)` holds, so arena_reset_rejects_live_dependents_underInv does not apply.",
    "fix": "Make the reset obligation or ResetPre also cover every active authority derived from `internal` over the storage, not only the entries of `ar.issued`. Otherwise report the gap in (d)/(e) together with decision (c) 14."
   },
   {
    "title": "With the root-authority clause in TransferPre, an arena returned from a call is dead: §7 `arena = create_arena()` can no longer be represented, and the report does not say so",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:461 (TransferPre, `s.org b ≠ none`); report formal/reports/MM03_v0.1.md:32, :160-161 ((c) 12), :231 ((e) 5)",
    "cause": "An interpretation whose consequence is not reported. Under arbitrage 3, `internal` is a root authority held by the abstraction. The new clause forbids any root in `auths`, so `internal` keeps the callee's frame and exitFrame restitutes it. The leak the fix closes is real, because the storage is a callee local. But (c) 12 does not state the consequence, and (e) 5 says the §7 scenario succeeds.",
    "evidence": "Spec §7: `arena = create_arena()` … « Le modèle doit permettre ce scénario lorsque buffer n'est plus utilisable au moment du reset ».\n\nLean witness /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/review2/fixlens/CreateArena.lean (compiles without error).     "fix": "In (c) 12 or (e), state that abstractions holding a root `internal` cannot be returned or moved across frames. State also that §7 is represented only with `create_arena` inlined in the caller's frame, and submit the question of durable abstraction storage for arbitration."
   },
   {
    "title": "The new ArenaInv still accepts an arena whose metadata and storage are under the same root (anchor derived from internal)",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:2076-2077 (ArenaInv, clauses added in 000fc59); report :35",

    "evidence": "Arbitrage 3: « le stockage administré est sous une autorité racine séparée (internal_authority) ». Arbitrage 2: « Chaque emplacement a une autorité racine ». Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

## Lean

- The Lake project is in `formal/`. `formal/DESIGN.md` governs how to formalize, never what the semantics is. Propose design decisions it does not settle in your report; never take them silently.
- Every definition or theorem that encodes a spec rule cites the rule's location in its docstring.
- A definition says what its rule says. Never make a definition more permissive, add an unjustified hypothesis or narrow a theorem's domain to obtain a proof.
- Never change a theorem statement, or a definition it depends on, to make a proof go through. If stuck, stop and report the goal state.
- Never use `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `native_decide`.

## Report

Spec passages implemented (by location), what changed, what is unproven or open, spec problems found.

Adversarial and read-only. For each change, check:

- It says exactly what the spec says: not stronger, not weaker. Read definitions, hypotheses and quantifiers, not only proofs. A theorem that holds because a definition is too permissive or its hypotheses are unsatisfiable is blocking.
- Each formalized rule cites its spec location.
- No theorem statement or dependency was changed without the task allowing it.
- No interpretation was chosen silently where the spec is unclear.
- Nothing outside the task was added.

When a milestone is declared complete, compare the rules in its announced scope with the spec locations cited in `formal/`, and list every rule left without a definition or theorem.

Every finding needs evidence: a spec quote, a counterexample or command output. No evidence, no finding. Never ask for additions beyond the task.

Output: verdict (block / changes / ok), then each finding with severity, location, cause (formalization error, missing coverage or spec defect) and evidence.
